intro: Picture a small resort in central Hua Hin with a pool set in a leafy garden, rooms designed around the sea, the sand and the sunshine, and a beach just a few hundred metres away on foot — Escape Hua Hin is a 4-star boutique resort in the Sansiri Hotel Collection, set right on Phetchkasem Road in the heart of the Hua Hin beach area · What many guests talk about is how calm and tucked-away it feels, almost like escaping the town, even though it's close to everything, and how reasonable the price is for a resort in such a good spot · 46 rooms, from about ฿2,000/night · 9.3 from 188 reviews on Trip.com · Important to know: the hotel was renovated and renamed The Peri Hotel Hua Hin back in 2020, but it's still searched for and booked under the name Escape Hua Hin on many platforms

body.html: Who Escape Hua Hin is for — to put it as simply as possible, Escape Hua Hin is a small boutique resort for people who want to "escape the chaos" and unwind by the sea in Hua Hin without paying five-star beachfront prices · It isn't a high-rise hotel with hundreds of rooms, and it isn't a beachfront property where you open the door onto the sand · Instead it's a small resort of just 46 rooms in the Sansiri Hotel Collection, with low-rise buildings arranged around a pool in a leafy garden, which gives it a private, quiet feel even though it sits in the middle of the Hua Hin beach area on Phetchkasem Road · Real reviews line up on this: the people who suit it best are couples after a quiet, romantic mood, small families bringing children to play in the pool, and travellers who want a slow, unhurried break — more than anyone chasing grand luxury or every facility you'd get at a big resort · Key thing to understand first: this hotel was originally called Escape Hua Hin, one of Sansiri's resorts, but in 2020 it went through a major renovation and was rebranded as The Peri Hotel Hua Hin, under a theme inspired by Hemingway's novel The Old Man and the Sea, in blue and white · So if you search for Escape Hua Hin and the name The Peri Hotel comes up, don't be confused — it's the same place at the same location, just renovated and renamed

Location and getting around — Escape Hua Hin sits on Phetchkasem Road in the heart of the Hua Hin beach area, a location that scores very highly in reviews (Trip.com rates the location category as high as around 9.7) · The standout is that the beach is about 200 m away on foot, just a few minutes, so you can head out for an early-morning stroll along the sea or a swim without driving · The hotel is also close to Hua Hin's main eating and sightseeing spots — only a few minutes' walk to a short drive from BlúPort Hua Hin Resort Mall, and not far from the Hua Hin night market, Chatchai Market and the historic Hua Hin railway station · Going further afield is easy too, since it's on Phetchkasem Road, the main route, so grabbing a ride or driving to Hua Hin Floating Market, Vana Nava Water Jungle or Cicada Market isn't hard · Getting here from Bangkok is among the easiest of any beach town — about a 2.5–3 hour drive, or several minivan/coach departures a day · One small note: the hotel fronts onto Phetchkasem Road, a big road, so rooms facing the road may catch some traffic noise at certain times, but because the layout wraps the buildings around an inner garden, most rooms are fairly quiet

"I love that it's a small, quiet resort, just a few minutes' walk to the beach. The pool in the middle of the garden is gorgeous and you can sit by it all day · For this price in Hua Hin, the atmosphere you get is great value."

Room types and decor — Escape Hua Hin has 46 rooms in all, spread across several low-rise buildings around the pool and garden · What makes the resort interesting is the room design built around a Sea, Sand and Sun theme with a fishing-village feel, using bright natural colours in the Escape era and shifting to a rustic blue-white-cream palette in The Peri era that looks clean and feels coastal · The main room types are the Superior Room (about 31–33 sqm) with a garden view, the Deluxe Poolside (about 30–35 sqm) looking out onto the pool and garden — a favourite in reviews because you can step straight from the room down to the pool — plus twin-bed and double-bed options to suit different groups · For families or larger groups there's the Two Bedroom Suite at about 104–126 sqm with a roomy living area, and a pet-friendly room (about 35 sqm) for guests who want to bring their dog or cat · Many reviews agree the rooms are clean (Trip.com rates cleanliness around 9.4), the beds are comfortable, and there's a balcony or sitting corner that helps you relax · One thing to note: because these are older buildings that have been renovated, some rooms may mix old and new details, and the room size is just right rather than huge like the suites at a luxury resort, so if a pool view matters to you it's worth requesting a Poolside room when you book

Facilities and the pool — the most talked-about highlight at Escape Hua Hin is the outdoor pool set in the middle of a leafy garden, ringed by large trees with a koi pond nearby · Many reviews say this pool is the spot that makes you want to sit and relax all day — calm, photogenic, and not crowded because there aren't many rooms · There's a separate kids' pool so families with little ones can let them play with peace of mind · Beyond the pool there's a fitness room, a spa/massage and a sauna for anyone who wants to unwind, including the massage service that's part of the charm of a Hua Hin-style break · For general facilities there's free Wi-Fi everywhere, free parking, room service, a tour desk to help arrange trips and call a ride, and a lobby lounge · To be straight about it, the pool here is more for soaking and relaxing than a lap pool for serious swimming, the hotel doesn't run an airport shuttle according to current information, and as a small resort it doesn't have every single facility a big resort would — but in terms of atmosphere and privacy it does very well at this price

Food and bar — the hotel's main restaurant is CHOW MONG, which in the local tongue means "fisherman" — a poolside seafood restaurant designed to feel like a modern fisherman's kitchen, casual with a garden view, good for eating with family or a group of friends · The signature menu focuses on fresh seafood, from seafood steamboat to grilled and steamed dishes · Reviews often praise the breakfast, which many say is "tastier and more generous than expected" for a small resort, with both Thai and international choices and fresh ingredients · There's also a bar/lounge and a café from the Peri era that add a spot to sip coffee and evening drinks · For other meals the hotel's location helps a lot, since it sits in the middle of the Hua Hin beach area where a few minutes' walk gets you to seafood spots, beachside restaurants and plenty of street-food markets, so many people choose to eat out and alternate with dining at the hotel · Overall the food here is a strong add-on, especially the breakfast and the poolside setting that fits the resort's coastal theme

Service — service is another point that earns consistent praise in real reviews · The staff here are often described as friendly, smiling, attentive and helpful, the kind of charm you find at a small resort where the team can look after every guest properly · Many people say it feels like a warm, easy welcome that isn't overly formal · The tour desk readily suggests places to visit, books restaurants and calls a ride · To be straight about it, because it's a small resort with limited staff, some services may involve a wait when the hotel is full, and there's no butler-level service like a luxury resort · But overall service is a strong point that leaves many guests impressed and wanting to come back

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulled together from Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a great location within walking distance of the beach and close to BlúPort, a quiet and private tucked-away atmosphere, a lovely leafy garden pool, clean rooms, friendly attentive staff, a tasty generous breakfast, and excellent value for the location and atmosphere you get · On the watch-out side: it comes up that this is a small resort, so it doesn't have every facility a big resort would, and it isn't directly on the beach (about a 200 m walk) · Some reviews mention the buildings and certain details showing their age, even after the renovation in the Peri era · There's traffic noise from Phetchkasem Road in road-facing rooms, and no airport shuttle · On top of that, the confusion between the names Escape Hua Hin and The Peri Hotel throws some people off when booking · Most of these gripes can be managed by setting the right expectation — that you're staying at a small resort with a nice atmosphere, not a large luxury beachfront resort

"The staff are lovely, the breakfast is tastier than the price suggests, and the rooms are clean · The only downside is it isn't right on the beach, so there's a little walk, and at first I was confused why I'd booked under the name Escape but the sign out front said The Peri — turns out it's the same place, newly renovated."

Price and value — Escape Hua Hin / The Peri Hotel starts at around ฿2,000/night for a Superior room on promotion or at the regular rate, rising to roughly ฿2,500–4,000+ for a Deluxe Poolside in high season or over long weekends · A two-bedroom suite for families sits in a higher range by size · Compared with central Hua Hin beach resorts in the same class, Escape Hua Hin feels like strong value among reasonably priced boutique resorts, especially once you factor in a location within walking distance of the beach and the mall, the private garden-pool atmosphere, and the well-reviewed breakfast · If you're planning a relaxed Hua Hin break and using the hotel as a base to walk around and eat by the beach, this resort feels like better value than paying a premium for a five-star resort whose facilities you may not fully use · But if you want a room right on the beach where you open the door onto the sand, or a full set of facilities, you may have to pay more for a beachfront resort directly

What to know before you book — a few things help your stay go smoothly · One, be clear on the name — Escape Hua Hin is now The Peri Hotel Hua Hin at the same location, renovated and renamed back in 2020, so check the photos and address (Phetchkasem Road) match before you book · Two, if you want a pool-view atmosphere, request a Deluxe Poolside room when you book · Three, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for an inner room that doesn't face Phetchkasem Road · Four, the hotel isn't directly on the beach — it's about a 200 m walk, so be ready for that and plan a morning or evening stroll down to the sand · Five, the hotel has no airport shuttle, so if you're coming from Bangkok, plan a minivan, coach or your own car · Six, in high season (November–February) and over long weekends Hua Hin fills up fast and prices climb, so book ahead and pick free cancellation if your plans aren't firm

Bottom line — across all the real reviews, Escape Hua Hin (now The Peri Hotel Hua Hin) is the boutique resort that suits people who want to unwind by the sea in Hua Hin in a quiet, private setting, on a budget that's within reach · The leafy garden pool, the clean and inviting Sea/Sand/Sun rooms, the friendly staff, the well-reviewed breakfast, and a location within walking distance of the beach and BlúPort make it good value in its price range · If you're after a large resort right on the beach where you open the door onto the sand, with every facility or five-star service, this may not be the answer, and you should look at a beachfront resort directly instead · But for a relaxing Hua Hin trip where you want a calm atmosphere in a lively area, along with good value and a warm welcome — Escape Hua Hin meets that need well, and it's why it still holds high review scores even after the name change

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Escape Hua Hin

faq.q: Are Escape Hua Hin and The Peri Hotel Hua Hin the same place?
faq.a: Yes — it's the same place at the same location on Phetchkasem Road · It was originally called Escape Hua Hin, one of the resorts in the Sansiri Hotel Collection · In 2020 it went through a major renovation and was rebranded as The Peri Hotel Hua Hin under an Old Man and the Sea theme in blue and white · But many platforms still let you search for and book it under the name Escape Hua Hin

faq.q: Where is Escape Hua Hin · can you walk to the beach?
faq.a: The hotel is at 25/2 Phetchkasem Road in the heart of the Hua Hin beach area, Hua Hin district, Prachuap Khiri Khan province · The beach is about 200 m away on foot, just a few minutes · It's close to BlúPort Hua Hin mall and not far from the night market, Hua Hin railway station and the town-centre eating and sightseeing spots

faq.q: What's the starting price at Escape Hua Hin · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿2,000/night for a Superior room on promotion or at the regular rate · There's a Deluxe Poolside with a pool view, a Pet-Friendly room that welcomes pets, and a Two Bedroom Suite of about 104–126 sqm for families · Prices in high season (Nov–Feb) and over long weekends climb fast, so it's worth comparing several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is Escape Hua Hin good for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, small families and travellers who want to unwind by the sea in Hua Hin in a quiet setting on a budget that's within reach · There's a leafy garden pool, a private atmosphere, and a location within walking distance of the beach · If you're after a large resort directly on the beach or a full set of facilities, another beachfront resort may suit you better

faq.q: Does Escape Hua Hin welcome pets · is breakfast included?
faq.a: There's a Pet-Friendly Deluxe room of about 35 sqm that welcomes pets for guests bringing their dog or cat (it's worth checking the terms with the hotel before booking) · And breakfast is included in many packages and is praised in reviews for being tasty and varied, with both Thai and international choices, served at CHOW MONG by the pool

faq.q: Does Escape Hua Hin have an airport shuttle?
faq.a: According to current information, the hotel has no airport shuttle service · If you're travelling from Bangkok, plan to come by minivan, coach or your own car (about 2.5–3 hours) · The hotel has a tour desk that can call a ride and advise on getting around the area
